name: Midges
note: Midges (docs 11, 12): not a creature with needs, arrival or trust but an ecology field, one share per square meter, that frogs eat (and later minnows, dragonflies and bats). field (S6a, the hourly tick): midges gather over still fresh water and the ground within nearWaterM of it, where plants feed them: each plant's weight (feed; a clump counts its size, a cover plant its share) is summed over a square of feedRadiusM, and fullFeed of it gives the most midges there can be. warmth scales that by season (spring, summer, autumn, winter). Each hour the field moves riseShare of the way up toward it, or fallShare of the way down, so a new reed bed fills with midges over a day or so and a drained one empties faster. A new world starts with none. When the journal first knows them is in recipes/world/journal.json (midges.seenAt). swarm: the live look for S6b, from Matt's pond tier 1 prototype (drawn from this field, more at dusk, fewer at night and in wind).
